question: I have a valid Ontario health card. Should I assume that an ordinary dental cleaning at a dentist's office will be covered by OHIP?
generated_answer:

Dental Care for Children and Youth - Children and youth up to 17 years of age may be eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP).

Dental Care for Adults Receiving Ontario Works or the Ontario Disability Support Program - Adults who are recipients of Ontario Works or the Ontario Disability Support Program are eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP).

Dental Care for Ontario Seniors - Adults 65 years of age and older may be eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP). To find out if you are eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), please call ServiceOntario at 1-800-206-6153 (toll-free) or 416-327-4198 (Toronto area) or visit the ServiceOntario Centre. The centre will be able to confirm your eligibility for dental services. When you contact ServiceOntario, please have the following information ready:

your full name and address

date of birth

family information

social insurance number

proof of residence

If you are eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), you will need to provide your health card number and the name and address of your dentist. If you are not eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), you will need to provide your health card number and the name and address of your dentist, as well as a letter from your dentist explaining why you are not eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP).

If you are not eligible for dental services under the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), you may still be eligible for other types of dental coverage.
